7 components, 4 nets. A textbook single-loop circuit, not a random ladder: a 50V source feeding 1k in series into a node that drives a 10mH inductor to ground and a parallel 2k || 30uF pair, whose far side drives 6k to ground. The tracer's default netlist was already correct; nothing needed overriding, but every site was checked and is recorded explicitly.

NET MAP
  n3 = V-DC #3 top / '+' lead (128,454) up the left rail to (128,380) and right to Resistor #1 (1k) left lead (182,379). 2 terminals.
  n1 = the middle node. Resistor #1 right lead (297,385) runs right along y~384 through S7 (326,385) and into S6 (378,382); S7 drops a branch down x~330 to Inductor #4 top (330,491); S6 sits on the vertical at x~378 that runs from y~300 down to y~445, feeding Resistor #0 (2k) left lead (456,300) along the top and Capacitor #2 (30uF) left lead (476,442) along the bottom. Terminals: 1.1, 4.0, 0.0, 2.0.
  n2 = the right node. Resistor #0 right lead (567,312) runs right to the corner (652,300) and down the x~652 vertical through S11 (652,444), where Capacitor #2's right lead (574,446) joins, and on down to Resistor #5 (6k) top lead (649,500). Terminals: 0.1, 2.1, 5.0. This is the node where 2k and 30uF are in parallel.
  0  = the bottom rail y~672-676, from V-DC #3 bottom lead (124,590) down to (124,672) and right through S16 (340,674, Inductor #4 bottom lead 339,615 coming down), S18 (407,676, where GND #6's lead 406,681 drops), and on to Resistor #5 bottom lead (642,622). Terminals: 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 6.0.

SITE DECISIONS
  All eleven sites are junctions; there is not one ambiguous crossing on this sheet - no wire crosses another anywhere, every site is a T where a branch terminates on a through-running wire.
  S6 (378,382) CRITICAL: the y~384 wire from Resistor #1 lands on the middle of the x~378 vertical that spans y=300..445. Crossing here is not even expressible (deg3); a 'none' would strand the whole 2k/30uF block. Junction.
  S7 (326,385) CRITICAL: the branch down to Inductor #4 leaves the y~384 wire. Junction; otherwise Inductor #4's top would be a one-terminal net.
  S11 (652,444) CRITICAL: Capacitor #2's right lead lands on the x~652 vertical. Junction; otherwise 2.1 would be a one-terminal net.
  S16 (340,674) CRITICAL: Inductor #4's bottom lands on the bottom rail (with a small ink blob). Junction.
  S18 (407,676) CRITICAL: GND #6's lead drops off the bottom rail; deg4 only because the GND symbol's top bar sits just under it. Junction - this is what puts the rail on net '0'.
  Non-critical S2 (524,345) and S3 (516,346) are the '2kOhm' label brushing Resistor #0's box; S8 (195,412) and S10 (226,428) are the '1kOhm' label under Resistor #1; S13 (568,501) is the 'uF' of '30uF'; S15 (681,564) is the '6' of '6kOhm' touching Resistor #5. None of them can change the netlist (the wires they touch are already the same net) and all are left at the default.

PORTS / CLASSES
  No port fixes were needed. Every warned-about extra port is handwriting: Resistor #0 (502,337)/(535,337) = '2kOhm'; Resistor #1 (217,415)/(234,414)/(200,411)/(190,414) = '1kOhm'; Capacitor #2 (479,491) = the '3' of '30uF'; V-DC #3 (184,561) = the '5' of '50V'; Resistor #5 (684,563) = the '6' of '6kOhm'. In every case the two real leads were already selected.
  All 7 classes accepted; each symbol is unambiguous (two zigzag resistors drawn horizontally, one vertically, a coil inductor, a parallel-plate capacitor, a circled +/- DC source, a three-bar ground).
  V-DC #3 terminal order left at the default (t0 = top, the '+' plate; t1 = bottom, on ground) - order is not scored for a 2-terminal part, but it happens to match the drawn polarity.
  The rectangle around the whole drawing (x 10..1010, y 275..745) is the page border, not a wire. It carries no terminal and forms no net; it is visible as the green outline in the overview and was correctly ignored.

UNRESOLVED
